# Maxwell

> The session manager for Claude Code. A native Mac app.

## Getting started

- [Install and update](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/install): Maxwell runs on a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. You also need Claude Code.
- [Start and bring in sessions](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/first-session): Sessions you start in Maxwell are Claude Code background sessions. They keep running when Maxwell closes or crashes.

## Sessions

- [Session groups](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/groups): Every session is in exactly one group, picked by what it needs from you. You only have to look at the first two.
- [Safe to close](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/safe-to-close): Closing a session that's still working, or waiting on you, costs you work. So Maxwell only calls a session safe when it can prove it.
- [Cloud sessions](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/cloud): Claude Code can run a session on Anthropic's cloud machines instead of your Mac. Maxwell starts them, lists them with your other sessions, and moves work there and back.
- [Session names](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/session-names): A session keeps Claude's title when that title says something. Otherwise Maxwell names the task once, so every row reads at a glance.
- [Projects and the rail](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/projects): Each session belongs to a project, its git repo by default. A rail on the left, like the macOS Dock, switches between them.
- [Search and actions](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/search): One box finds any session, project or action. Press ⌘P, or Shift twice.

## Workspace

- [Panels and layout](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/panels): Sessions, usage, system and plugins are panels that sit left, right or bottom. The viewer stays on the right, beside its session.
- [Files and artifacts](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/viewer): Files and claude.ai artifacts a session writes open on the right, beside the session that made them.
- [Accounts and usage](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/accounts): Maxwell reads every Claude Code account on your Mac and shows how much room each one has left.
- [Themes and appearance](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/appearance): Themes come in a light and dark pair and follow macOS. Graphite, Silver and Paper ship with Maxwell.
- [Voice mode](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/voice): Maxwell says which session needs you. You answer out loud, and your words are typed into it.

## Plugins

- [Linear](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/linear): The Linear plugin shows which ticket each session works on, and keeps its status current.
- [Slack](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/slack): The Slack plugin lists who is waiting on a reply from you. It reads only, and never posts, reacts or drafts.
- [Write a plugin](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/write-a-plugin): A plugin is a folder with a manifest and a program, in any language. It talks to Maxwell with JSON lines over stdin and stdout.

## Reference

- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/keyboard-shortcuts): Every action has a key, and every key can be changed in Settings › Keys or with a keybind line.
- [Configuration](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/configuration): One plain text file, one key = value per line. Maxwell reloads it the moment you save, and the Settings window writes the same file.
- [Command line](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/command-line): The Maxwell binary answers a few commands in a terminal, for auditing and undoing.
- [What Maxwell touches](https://www.runmaxwell.com/docs/privacy): Everything stays on your Mac. Maxwell sends nothing anywhere, apart from the Haiku reads and the cloud session listing, which go through your own Claude account, crash reports you can turn off, and what plugins you turn on.
